findings.F1: The book's gain rests on one window. w16 holds 0.2337 of the book's summed daily return of 0.2439 across the twelve windows of folds B and C. Its 13 cases short-move +24.8 % over 5 days (t 5.96) and its 15 trades net +23.98 % on average. With w16 left out, the Sharpe falls to 0.074, against 0.45 to 0.52 when any other window is left out. This is what fails "lowest Sharpe, one window left out", and it drags the Calmar and the comparison with holding.
findings.F2: Outside w16 the idea's grading by the depth of the 5-day fall (in recent-swing units) is inverted, and the sizing follows it.
findings.F3: How near the close sits to the day's high grades the move the way the brief's theory says. On the quartile of cases with the close nearest the high (median location 0.89), the short 5-day move is +6.95 % (t 3.06, 23 cases), against +5.38 %, +5.13 % and +1.59 % on the lower quartiles (median locations 0.57, 0.68, 0.80). The lowest quartile is not the smallest, so the grading is not monotone. This was not measured with w16 left out.
findings.F4: How wide the day's range is against its 20-day average also grades the move.

findings.F6: The move builds over the 5-day horizon and gives part back after it: +2.56 % at 1 day, +2.87 % at 2, +4.25 % at 3, +4.79 % at 5 (t 3.49, 89 cases), and +1.64 % at 10 days. The 5-day holding (trades last 4.1 to 5.1 days) is right. The grading, not the horizon, is what the repair must change.

ideas.idea: In a choppy, agitated market, when a coin's daily close sits in the upper part of that day's high-low range after its 5-day return has been negative, its price falls over the next five days, and the nearer that close is to the day's high, the larger the fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader sizes the short by how tightly the close is pinned to the day's high rather than by the depth of the 5-day fall, which put most of the book's size on cases that paid in one window only.
ideas.name: high-pinned close fades

ideas.idea: In a choppy, agitated market, when a coin's daily close sits in the upper part of that day's high-low range after its 5-day return has been negative, its price falls over the next five days, and the wider that day's high-low range against its average range over the last 20 days, the larger the fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader leans the short toward the days whose upper close came with an unusually wide day, where the late push was largest, and keeps little on narrow days, instead of loading on the deepest 5-day falls.
ideas.name: wide-day upper-close fade
